note: Lexikon der Wehrmacht (after Tessin): the 47th Volksgrenadier Division was formed on 17 September 1944 at Aarhus as the replacement of the destroyed 47th Infantry Division by renaming the 577th Grenadier Division, and the remnants of the 47th Infantry Division were incorporated.

Lexikon der Wehrmacht: the remnants of the 272nd Infantry Division marched to Döberitz to refit, where the division was re-formed from 17 September 1944 as the 272nd Volksgrenadier Division (by renaming the 575th Volksgrenadier Division, then forming).

Lexikon der Wehrmacht: the 277th Volksgrenadier Division was formed on 4 September 1944 in Hungary by renaming the 574th Volksgrenadier Division, then forming; the remnants of the 277th Infantry Division, collected at Stolberg near Aachen, were sent to it.
Lexikon der Wehrmacht (347th Volksgrenadier Division page): on 7 May 1945 the 347th Infantry Division was renamed the 347th Volksgrenadier Division.

Lexikon der Wehrmacht (after Tessin): the 352nd Volksgrenadier Division was formed on 21 September 1944 near Flensburg as the re-formation of the 352nd Infantry Division from the remnants of the old division and the 581st Volksgrenadier Division (32nd wave); Grenadier Regiments 914 to 916 kept their numbers. A US archival unit history (maparchive.ru) dates the re-formation 14 September 1944.

Lexikon der Wehrmacht: the 363rd Volksgrenadier Division was formed on 17 September 1944 at Wildflecken as the replacement of the destroyed 363rd Infantry Division from the 566th Volksgrenadier Division and the remnants of the 363rd Infantry Division.
Lexikon der Wehrmacht: the 462nd Volksgrenadier Division arose at the beginning of November 1944 from the 462nd Infantry Division when it was transferred to the field army (Metz).

Panzer Brigade 107 was formed at Mielau from the remnants of the 25th Panzergrenadier Division (28 July 1944 per Wikipedia; from 1 August 1944 per Lexikon der Wehrmacht). In November 1944 the brigade returned to the rebuilt division; that return is not a lineage row (it would be a cycle) and is described in unit_note.
Panzer Group West was renamed Fifth Panzer Army: 5 August 1944 per Breakout and Pursuit ch. 22 (preferred), 1 August 1944 per Wikipedia (conflict group G020).

Lexikon der Wehrmacht (165th Reserve Division page): on 1 August 1944 the division was renamed the 70th Infantry Division; the 70th Infantry Division page: formed in the Netherlands from the staff of the 165th Reserve Division. Added in the placeholder promotion pass, wf-health-fixes, 9 November 2026, approved by Scott.

Lexikon der Wehrmacht: the 18th Volksgrenadier Division was formed on 2 September 1944 in Denmark (renaming the 571st Volksgrenadier Division, as replacement for the 18th Infantry Division) and took over about 2,500 men of the 18th Luftwaffe Field Division; the 18th Luftwaffe Field Division page: only remnants of the division, destroyed in the Mons pocket in early September 1944, were used for the 18th Volksgrenadier Division. Added in the placeholder promotion pass, wf-health-fixes, 9 November 2026, approved by Scott.

Lexikon der Wehrmacht (Division Nr. 905 page): on 26 March 1945 the remnants of the division, assembled at Weingarten after crossing the Rhine at Neupotz, were merged into the 16th Volksgrenadier Division. Added in the theater and placeholder pass, branch placeholders-14-theater, 9 November 2026, approved by Scott.

FMS B-745 (German p.7 and Anlage 1): early in April 1945 the Nineteenth Army reorganised Division Nr. 405 into the 719th Infantry Division (the chart of 18 April lists "719. I.D., bisher Div.Nr.405"); Lexikon der Wehrmacht (Division Nr. 405 page): shortly before the end of the war the remnants of the division were used to form the 719th Infantry Division. The day is not given (12 April still Division Nr. 405 in the chart). Added in the theater and placeholder pass, branch placeholders-14-theater, 9 November 2026, approved by Scott.

Lexikon der Wehrmacht (Infanterie-Division Jütland page): on 3 August 1944 the shadow division was used, with the cadres of the 19th Luftwaffe Field Division, to form the 19th Grenadier Division (later the 19th Volksgrenadier Division) and was dissolved; it was formed again in Denmark on 9 March 1945 under the same record. Added in the theater and placeholder pass, branch placeholders-14-theater, 9 November 2026, approved by Scott.

Lexikon der Wehrmacht (after Tessin): the remnants of the 49th Infantry Division were incorporated into the newly re-formed 246th (Volksgrenadier) Division; by order of 5 December 1944 (Nr. I/20998/44) the 49th Infantry Division counted as disbanded with immediate effect. End of the record added in consistency fix 3. Added in the consistency pass, branch wf-consistency-fixes, 9 November 2026, approved by Scott.

Lexikon der Wehrmacht (after Tessin): in mid-November 1944 XIII SS Corps ordered the broken 48th Infantry Division disbanded and its remnants incorporated into the 559th Volksgrenadier Division (date entered as mid-month). End of the record added in consistency fix 3. Added in the consistency pass, branch wf-consistency-fixes, 9 November 2026, approved by Scott.

Lexikon der Wehrmacht (after Tessin): the division was officially disbanded on 4 August 1944; its infantry went to the 21st Panzer Division and the other parts to the forming 16th Infantry Division. End of the record added in consistency fix 3. Added in the consistency pass, branch wf-consistency-fixes, 9 November 2026, approved by Scott.

Lexikon der Wehrmacht (after Tessin): in mid-March 1945 the division was disbanded and its remnants joined with those of the 26th Volksgrenadier Division in one battle group (date entered as mid-month). End of the record added in consistency fix 3. Added in the consistency pass, branch wf-consistency-fixes, 9 November 2026, approved by Scott.

Lexikon der Wehrmacht (after Tessin): after refitting the brigade was again put under the 9th Panzer Division, and the bulk of the brigade was transferred into the 9th Panzer Division in October 1944 (month only). End of the record added in consistency fix 3. Added in the consistency pass, branch wf-consistency-fixes, 9 November 2026, approved by Scott.

Hunt-class destroyer launched as HMS Bedale on 23 July 1941 and commissioned into the Polish Navy as ORP Ślązak (L26) before completion, in April 1942. Wikipedia gives the commissioning on 17 April 1942 and the Polish Navy Museum gives 30 April 1942; the month is entered because the two sources disagree on the day (lineage rows have no alternates). Added in the air-naval pilot (branch air-naval-pilot, 13 November 2026): old value none, new value this lineage row.
